title: 4 Days in Las Vegas
subtitle: The Strip, Valley of Fire & Fremont Street
summary: Four days and three nights based at The Venetian: a Styx concert, Meow Wolf's Omega Mart, a day among the red rocks of Valley of Fire, desert art south of town, steakhouse dinners and the best free spectacles on the Strip.

glance.label: Day trip
glance.value: Valley of Fire State Park, 1 hour northeast of the Strip

glance.label: Getting around
glance.value: Rental car for the desert, walking and Uber on the Strip

glance.label: Highlights
glance.value: Styx at the Venetian Theater, Omega Mart, the Fire Wave, Seven Magic Mountains

intro: This Las Vegas trip balanced the iconic with the unexpected: a Styx concert at the Venetian Theater, immersive art at Meow Wolf's Omega Mart, the jaw-dropping red rock landscape of Valley of Fire, steakhouse dinners, an ice bar, and the best free spectacles on the Strip. Four days, three nights, one rental car, and a lot of ground to cover.

We made The Venetian our home base. The Grand Canal Shoppes, Grand Lux Cafe and Rosina Cocktail Lounge are all steps from the room, and the Strip in both directions is walkable from the front entrance. The rental car stayed in the free self-park garage for our early desert mornings: Valley of Fire on Sunday, then Seven Magic Mountains and Jean Dry Lake Bed on Monday.

days_plan.label: Day 1
days_plan.title: Arrival day – welcome to Vegas
days_plan.text: An evening flight, a rental car, and a first look at the Strip before an early night. Saturday is a full day.

items.text: Fly from Newark to Harry Reid International (LAS)
Take the rental car shuttle from the terminal and pick up the car we'd use for all three desert outings
Check in at The Venetian, then a short stroll through the Grand Canal Shoppes or along the Strip – even 20 minutes sets the tone for the weekend

days_plan.tip: The Venetian's attached self-park garage is free for hotel guests; we used it instead of valet to keep the car handy for early departures.

days_plan.label: Day 2
days_plan.title: Omega Mart, the Strip & Styx
days_plan.text: A morning inside Meow Wolf's surreal supermarket, a free-spectacle walk down the Strip, burgers at the Flamingo, and Styx at the Venetian Theater.

items.text: Breakfast at Grand Lux Cafe, right inside the Venetian – the Cheesecake Factory's upscale sibling, with a big all-day menu
Meow Wolf Omega Mart at Area 15 (timed entry, a 10-minute drive) – an immersive art world hidden inside a surreal supermarket. Allow at least 90 minutes, follow the story and open every door
Explore the rest of Area 15 with Level 0 passes – more immersive installations, axe throwing, VR and more, if energy allows
Supply run for water and snacks (for the room and for Valley of Fire), then freshen up at the hotel

Strip walk: Palazzo shops → Wynn Conservatory (free seasonal floral display) → coffee at Urth Caffé → the Forum Shops at Caesars (Trevi Fountain replica and animated Roman statues) → the free Flamingo Wildlife Habitat
Dinner at Gordon Ramsay Burger at the Flamingo – the Hell's Kitchen burger and truffle fries are the standouts
More Strip exploring on the way back toward the Venetian, including the Bellagio Fountains (every 15 minutes after 8 PM)
Styx at the Venetian Theater
A round on the Venetian casino floor or a drink at Rosina Cocktail Lounge before calling it a night

days_plan.tip: The Flamingo Wildlife Habitat is free and genuinely surprising – Chilean flamingos, African penguins and koi behind a casino. Easy to spend 20 minutes there.

days_plan.label: Day 3
days_plan.title: Valley of Fire & a night at The LINQ
days_plan.text: An early start for the desert light at Valley of Fire State Park, a picnic among the sandstone, the Fire Wave hike, then back to the Strip for steak, magic and the High Roller.

items.text: Quick Starbucks and pack all the water and snacks – the park has limited facilities
Drive about an hour northeast on I-15, then Route 169 into the park (entry fee at the gate)
Beehive Rock (~15 min) – sandstone cross-bedding whose grooves shift direction as you look
Atlatl Rock (~20 min) – petroglyphs carved 2,000–4,000 years ago, seen up close from a metal staircase
Picnic lunch at Seven Sisters (~40 min) among towering sandstone formations
Rainbow Vista (~15 min) – swirling, painted-looking rock and a short loop toward the Fire Canyon overlook
Fire Canyon Overlook (~10 min) – red-and-white sandstone with Silica Dome in the distance
Elephant Rock (~20 min) – a short walk to the best view of the park's most photogenic landmark
Fire Wave (~60 min) – the highlight: a striped red, white and pink sandstone wave, about 1.5 miles round trip, easy to moderate
Drive back to the Venetian to shower and change
Dinner at Smith & Wollensky's in the Grand Canal Shoppes – classic American steakhouse with an impressive wine list
Mat Franco – Magic Reinvented Nightly at The LINQ, the America's Got Talent winner's intimate magic show
Optional: Minus 5 Ice Bar at The LINQ – everything kept at -5°C, with thermal coats and gloves provided (about 45 minutes); the speakeasy next door is the warm alternative
High Roller Observation Wheel – 550 feet tall, a 30-minute rotation over the Strip lit up at night
Wind down at the Bellagio: the fountains and the free, 24/7 Conservatory, dressed for Lunar New Year

days_plan.tip: Bring at least 2 liters of water per person – the desert is dehydrating even in January. The Fire Wave photographs best when the sun is low, morning or late afternoon.

days_plan.label: Day 4
days_plan.title: Desert art, Fremont Street & a final dinner
days_plan.text: Early photos at Seven Magic Mountains and Jean Dry Lake Bed, lunch in the Arts District, a steakhouse send-off at the Venetian, and a last night downtown.

items.text: Quick Starbucks and go early – fewer people and better light
Seven Magic Mountains, about 30 minutes south on I-15 – Ugo Rondinone's seven neon-painted boulder towers, up to 35 feet tall. Free and open 24 hours
Jean Dry Lake Bed, a short drive away – a vast white playa for wide-open desert shots and long morning shadows
Welcome to Las Vegas sign, if there's room in the dedicated lot at the south end of the Strip
Pinball Hall of Fame (free to enter, pay per game) or PlayPlayground at Luxor, a multi-story interactive venue
Lunch at Esther's Kitchen in the Arts District – wood-fired, Italian-influenced cooking and excellent pasta
Optional Arts District stroll: Container Park and Ferguson's Motel
Back to the Venetian for the pool if it's heated and open – or last-minute Sphere tickets for The Wizard of Oz at 5 PM
Final dinner at Delmonico Steakhouse, Emeril Lagasse's flagship inside the Venetian

Uber downtown to the Fremont Street Experience: the free LED canopy shows on the hour, Don't Tell Mama piano bar, Vegas Vickie's Cocktail Lounge, the $1 million photo at Binion's, the Silver Strike coin machine and Pink Box Donuts at The Plaza, and the gold nugget at the Golden Nugget

days_plan.tip: Get to Seven Magic Mountains as early as you can – the low morning light makes the colors pop, and by 10 AM the tour groups often arrive.

stays.name: The Venetian
stays.note: Grand Canal Shoppes, Grand Lux Cafe, Rosina and Delmonico are all steps from the room, the Strip is walkable in both directions, and self-parking is free for hotel guests.

eats.name: Grand Lux Cafe
eats.note: The Cheesecake Factory's upscale concept with an extensive all-day menu – a proper sit-down breakfast without leaving the hotel. Walk in.

eats.name: Gordon Ramsay Burger
eats.note: Casual and satisfying, and exactly right before a two-hour concert. The Hell's Kitchen burger and truffle fries are the go-to order.

eats.name: Smith & Wollensky's
eats.note: Classic American steakhouse with excellent cuts and an impressive wine list. The dinner menu starts at 5 PM, so book for 5 or later if you want it.

eats.name: Esther's Kitchen
eats.note: One of Las Vegas's most acclaimed non-casino restaurants: wood-fired, Italian-influenced cooking, excellent pasta and a lively room. Off-Strip, so drive or Uber; reservation recommended.

eats.name: Delmonico Steakhouse
eats.note: Emeril Lagasse's flagship steakhouse – aged beef, Creole-influenced sides and a beautifully designed room. A strong, no-Uber-needed final dinner.

eats.name: Milk Bar
eats.note: Famous for Cereal Milk soft serve. Open late, inexpensive and genuinely delicious after the Bellagio fountains or a Strip walk.

eats.name: Rosina Cocktail Lounge
eats.note: Classic cocktails in a relaxed but upscale room – not a club, not a dive. Exactly the right vibe after a long day; no reservation needed.

eats.name: The Chandelier Lounge
eats.note: A stunning three-story lounge inside a massive chandelier installation. Craft cocktails and a grown-up energy – one of the best bars in Las Vegas.

eats.name: Skyfall Lounge
eats.note: A 64th-floor lounge with some of the best panoramic Strip views from any bar. Calm and grown-up – ideal for a sunset cocktail.

eats.name: Giordano's
eats.note: Chicago-style deep dish pizza – hearty and familiar for a casual dinner when nobody wants another steakhouse.

eats.name: Earl of Sandwich
eats.note: Hot pressed sandwiches, fast service and low prices – a reliable grab-and-go between Strip activities.

eats.name: Pink Box Donuts
eats.note: Creative donut flavors and an inexpensive stop during a Fremont Street evening.

book_ahead: The Venetian (or your Strip hotel of choice)
Rental car from Harry Reid airport – you'll need it for Valley of Fire, Seven Magic Mountains and Jean Dry Lake Bed
Concert tickets for the Venetian Theater
Meow Wolf Omega Mart at Area 15 (timed entry) and Area 15 Level 0 passes
Smith & Wollensky's, Esther's Kitchen and Delmonico Steakhouse (all on OpenTable)
Mat Franco – Magic Reinvented Nightly at The LINQ (sells out regularly)
High Roller Observation Wheel at The LINQ
Minus 5 Ice Bar time slot at The LINQ
PlayPlayground at Luxor (buy online in advance)
Sphere – last-minute tickets are sometimes available, so check the website or box office on the day
Lion Habitat Ranch and Red Door Escape Rooms, if you have extra time

tips.title: Rent a car for the desert
tips.text: The Strip is walkable and Uber covers the rest, but Valley of Fire, Seven Magic Mountains and Jean Dry Lake Bed all need a car. Pick it up via the rental car shuttle at Harry Reid and park free in the Venetian's self-park garage.

tips.title: Layer up in January
tips.text: Days run 55–62°F, which is comfortable for exploring, but nights can drop to 38°F. Desert mornings are cold and afternoons warm, so bring a proper jacket. Check whether the pool is heated before planning a swim.

tips.title: Prep for Valley of Fire
tips.text: It's an hour from the Strip with minimal facilities. Pack at least 2 liters of water per person plus snacks, bring sunscreen even in January, wear comfortable walking shoes for the Fire Wave, and have cash or card for the entry fee. Aim to leave by 9 AM for the best light.

tips.title: Mind the steakhouse menu switch
tips.text: Smith & Wollensky's serves its lunch menu until 5 PM. If you're booked earlier, ask to be seated closer to 5 or check with the host about the dinner menu.

tips.title: The best things on the Strip are free
tips.text: The Wynn Conservatory's seasonal display, the Forum Shops' Trevi Fountain, the Flamingo Wildlife Habitat, the Bellagio Fountains and Conservatory (open 24/7 – the Lunar New Year display is one of its best), and the Fremont Street canopy shows all cost nothing.

tips.title: Go early for desert photos
tips.text: Seven Magic Mountains is best in soft, low morning light before the tour groups arrive around 10 AM. The Fire Wave looks richest in the morning or late afternoon; midday light flattens the rock.

tips.title: If you have extra time
tips.text: Lion Habitat Ranch in Henderson is a nonprofit sanctuary for more than 40 African lions, and Red Door Escape Rooms at the Grand Bazaar Shops offers private rooms (Declassified, Enchantment or Survive). Book both in advance.
